nonrecommendation_reasons: Provider B is unbound; if no distinct provider is available or affordable, the cross-provider gate cannot execute without scope change.
Single clean reuse run (one fixture, one validator invocation) is minimal evidence of technical reuse generality; it does not cover alternate fixtures, commands, or environments.
No explicit timebox or cost cap is stated for Provider B onboarding, credentialing, or model access, which could delay or block execution.
The plan assumes the public wheel and fixture URLs remain stable and reachable; no fallback is defined if either artifact is removed or hash changes before execution.
corrections: Bind Provider B and model explicitly before execution authorization, including availability verification and cost ceiling.
Add a pre-execution liveness and hash check for both public URLs; if either fails, halt and re-scope rather than silently substituting artifacts.
Document a maximum elapsed-time and token-cost budget for the four model sessions to prevent unbounded spend on a recommendation-only validation.
review.rationale: The CE-G14 recommendation directly addresses the two material gaps left by CE-G13—provider dependence and unexecuted technical reuse—without expanding scope into platform features, commercial claims, or production readiness. The design is proportionate: two providers, four sessions, two public artifact fetches, and one clean synthetic reuse run. Authority boundaries are preserved, execution remains unauthorized, and non-claims are explicit. Residual risks (Provider B availability, artifact stability, minimal reuse coverage) are manageable with the suggested corrections and do not warrant withholding recommendation.
